questions.question: Q6. Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A) As of this article, the archive has just under 46,000 entries, from games to software you might have used growing up in school B) The digital revolution should have made preserving the past easier, but instead, it feels to me like we’ve only lost access. D) While there may be a host of sources on the web for finding old software, there’s perhaps no collection as complete as The Internet Archive: The non-profit has a collection of CD-ROM files that span decades.

D. While there may be a host of sources on the web for finding old software, there’s perhaps no collection as complete as The Internet Archive: The non-profit has a collection of CD-ROM files that span decades.
• This sentence introduces "The Internet Archive," providing the solution to the problem mentioned in the first two sentences and directly connecting to the hint from sentence C about knowing where to find the old software and games.
A. As of this article, the archive has just under 46,000 entries, from games to software you might have used growing up in school.
• This sentence gives further details about The Internet Archive, ending the paragraph on a note that ties back to the nostalgia implied in the previous sentences.

B) The platforms derive their power from not just connecting sellers and buyers, but also ensuring physical fulfillment of transactions or integrating online with offline. questions.questionHtml:
Q7. Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A) The success of Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), the government-backed online marketplace, will ultimately depend on its ability to facilitate, if not offer, end-to-end solutions from logistics and warehousing to delivery and payments.
B) The platforms derive their power from not just connecting sellers and buyers, but also ensuring physical fulfillment of transactions or integrating online with offline.
C) The likes of Amazon and Flipkart provide all these solutions, including through fulfillment centres receiving inbound products from vendors and ready for outbound dispatches whenever consumers order on their websites. That makes them, for all practical purposes, “operators” as opposed to mere online “platforms”.
D) E-commerce isn’t simply about placing orders for goods and services through digital platforms. Whatever is ordered online has to also be physically shipped and delivered in person to the buyer concerned.
questions.solution:
C) DACB
• Sentence D should be the first sentence because it introduces the concept of e-commerce and emphasizes that it isn't just about placing orders online. It establishes the context for the discussion that follows.
• Sentence A introduces the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) and mentions its success depending on its ability to facilitate or offer end-to-end solutions. This builds upon the introductory idea presented in sentence D, emphasizing the need for physical shipment and delivery.
• Sentence C should follow, as it provides concrete examples of platforms (Amazon and Flipkart) that provide all these solutions. It also introduces the contrast between "operators" and mere online "platforms", which is an important aspect of the argument that is being built up.
• Sentence B is the final sentence because it sums up the power and function of such platforms, which is not only connecting buyers and sellers but also ensuring physical fulfillment of transactions, a concept that has been developed throughout the preceding sentences. This conclusion echoes the ideas presented in the previous sentences and ties the paragraph together.

questions.questionHtml:
Q11. Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A) Data released by the National Statistical Office Friday showed that retail inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, has continued to trend lower, aided by a favourable base effect
B) Some analysts are now projecting inflation to remain below 5 per cent over the coming few months as well,
C) Inflation, which had edged above the Reserve Bank of India’s inflation targeting framework in January and February, falling thereafter to 5.66 per cent in March, declined further to an 18-month low of 4.7 per cent in April.

questions.solution:

• The paragraph is about inflation in India, as measured by the consumer price index, and its recent trends. The context is set by statements A and C which introduce the topic. Statement A sets the stage by stating that data released by the National Statistical Office shows that retail inflation is trending lower.

• Statement C follows naturally after A, as it provides more specific details about this trend, outlining how inflation rates have changed over recent months and emphasizing a decline to a significant 18-month low of 4.7 per cent in April.

• After setting the stage and providing a detailed trend analysis, statement B comes next as it projects future trends based on the current situation, stating that some analysts project that inflation will remain below 5 per cent over the coming few months.

• Finally, statement D wraps up the paragraph by offering a comparison of the current inflation rate to the previous forecast by the Reserve Bank of India, emphasizing how the current rate is lower than predicted.

questions.question: Comprehension: The screen flashes, and Bimal Roy's 'Do Bigha Zameen' comes to life with an opening scene of farmers anxiously looking at the sky. As the clouds gather, so do the farmers, expecting the rains to bestow their fields. It has been 70 years since Roy's classic, and this scene is as true of Indian farmers today as it was just after Independence, looking upward for innovations to empower them. Agriculture has been the backbone of sustenance and livelihood in India, marking a significant aspect of the country's socioeconomic landscape. With 55% of our population dependent on agriculture, it remains one of India's primary industries. Traditionally, farmers in India have encountered restricted access to credible information concerning the quality of agricultural input, including seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides. The farm-to-fork food value chain is extremely protracted and is riddled with multiple stakeholders who might not necessarily prioritize the welfare of farmers. This compels them to depend on local suppliers and intermediaries to procure such input, resulting in low valuation. Increasing intermediaries and other factors in this chain engender a reduction in transparency. As we head into our Amrit Kal, accompanied by their innovative digitized designs, AgriTech platforms emerge as the much-needed relief clouds, safeguarding farmers against unadulterated input. AgriTech platforms enable farmers to procure dependable and superior quality input by harnessing technological advancements such as data analytics and machine learning. These platforms safeguard farmers against the aforementioned malpractices by bridging the last mile between the suppliers and farmers via doorstep delivery, providing input from the factory to the farmer. Directly working with peer partners, retailers, and farmers, negotiating prices and dispatching goods, these platforms circumvent the involvement of intermediaries and local suppliers. Often classified under disruptive tech for having revolutionized the agriculture sector and existing procurement arrangements, AgriTech platforms procure high-quality input for farmers, including high-yielding varieties (HYV) seed, which has proven to be instrumental in driving up crop yields. In addition to providing farmers access to authentic and high-quality input, Agritech startups offer knowledge support by connecting them to experienced agronomists from the industry. By leveraging their expertise, AgriTech platforms guide farmers on the optimal selection of seed and agro-practices suitable for Indian and specifically regional farming conditions, thereby improving the likelihood of a successful harvest. The accessibility to such expert advice has been crucial in enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of farming practices, enabling farmers to make informed decisions and optimize their crop yields. Amidst a considerable emphasis on technology adoption in our contemporary era, Agritech Platforms have emerged as a catalyst in the endeavour to neutralize the effects of substandard inputs on farming. The potential for growth in the Indian Agrotech markets has become increasingly apparent, with an increasing number of startups entering the industry and building seamless digital platforms that can fully integrate value chains and fruitful harvests. With government support and the introduction of cutting-edge technologies such as 5G, these platforms have ripened a fertile ground for disruptive innovation in the agriculture sector. We may have come a long way from Do Bigha Zameen but aided with these platforms, the relief clouds may not be far away, and we might be looking at another revolution in India: one bought about by AgriTech. questions.question: Comprehension: Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it. I remain worried about my younger son. He is 12 years old and studying in 7th standard, addicted to online gaming. Though we set a timer on the tablet to monitor the usage he always exceeded the time limit. When my wife and I interrupt his gaming session or his broadband goes down, he responds with anger or rage-including shouting, screaming, or physical attacks, then this is something worth noting. A strong sense of urgency to get back to gaming remains there and it’s become difficult to pull him away. Many times, he skips his regular meals and relies on junk food and even resists taking toilet breaks. Compulsive play can manifest in playing past switch-off times, late at night, or secretively making it harder to get to sleep. The inappropriate violent or hateful content regularly in online gaming can take its toll on children’s well-being and growth and can lead to desensitization. I think this trauma is now a ‘Kahani Ghar-Ghar KI’. Three years back before Covid-19, my son was doing well in outdoor activities. He did skating for a few months and then switched over to cricket but as covid surged he had been forced to leave the outdoor activities. During Covid to continue their online mode of studies we bought a tablet for him. Unfortunately, he comes across inappropriate manners in exams also and begins to copy what his elder brother has done online. Many times simultaneously he uses two or more screens concurrently while in bed. I am talking about a mobile phone, a games console or a tablet maybe with a TV playing in the background but even so. Using a smartphone while watching TV or playing online games is becoming normal for him. The intention defines destiny. Seeing all this technology-led transformation in the surroundings, we recall our childhood days when there was a single black and white TV screen to watch ‘Chitrhaar’ on every Wednesday, and a movie on Sunday evening kept the families waiting for the whole week. In the last two decades as the technology buzz created, we all have to pay much more for it. The gully (streets) games like Gullidanda, Pakram-Pakrai (Hide and Seek) Staapu, Kho-kho, Kanche( small coloured glass balls), and many more traditional games which were good for physical and mental health, are nowhere around. However, every addiction is bad and best understood as a symptom rather than a problem. I tried a lot to reduce my son's online gaming by restricting access to devices, which probably won’t solve the problem permanently. To overcome gaming addiction and how to cope with it in healthier ways, it’s an important step for any child to acknowledge the consequences of harmful online gaming including cyberbullying, and how it is vulnerable to mental health like drug addiction causes isolation-affected relationships and education. Does ‘New India’ can spare its coming generation to be captured by the dopamine addiction to online gaming? How many productive hours do youths have and how are they spending these days? Are they spending their time in outdoor sports activities to improve their physical and mental fitness or are they spending on online games? A lasting recovery from gaming disorder comes through awareness at the school level itself and emotional resilience at home. A child needs to know how to recognize and handle emotional distress, anxiety, depression and overall loss of generation when they crave gameplay. The most significant way out is – That policymakers should come forward to curb dopamine-soaked online gaming through a policy imposing heavy usage charges linked to the time spent on gaming, which would force them automatically to get logged out in a few minutes.
